name: A Warden of the Horde

meta.previous: You Scream, I Scream... (Horde), Let's Go Fly a Kite (Horde)

summary: A Warden of the Horde concludes Children's Week by returning Grunth to Orphan Matron Battlewail in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself.

sections.title: An Orphan's Farewell
sections.body: After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks his guardian for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. Remembering his parents' advice to rise above hardship, he says he hopes to become a hero like the adventurer. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about their time together.

sections.title: Home to the Valley of Honor
sections.body: Returning to the orphanage in the Valley of Honor, adventurers return their young charge back into the care of Orphan Matron Battlewail. Taking responsibility for the young is considered a profound duty in the new Horde, where war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail commends your compassion as the true measure of a hero of the Horde, and Grunth parts ways with a beloved pet to ensure you remember the bond forged during your travels.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: This quest concludes the Horde's Children's Week festivities. Return Grunth and the Orcish Orphan Whistle to Orphan Matron Battlewail in the Valley of Honor.

Grunth is an orcish youth residing at the Orgrimmar Orphanage in the Valley of Honor. During Children's Week, he is paired with a Horde champion who takes him across Kalimdor to see legendary figures and grand sights.

faq.q: What do I bring back to the matron?
faq.answer: Bring the Orcish Orphan Whistle back to Orphan Matron Battlewail when Grunth is ready to return home.

faq.q: Who oversees the orphans in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Orphan Matron Battlewail manages the Orgrimmar Orphanage in the Valley of Honor, dedicating her life to sheltering and raising the Horde's war orphans.

faq.q: Why does Grunth want to return home?
faq.answer: His Children's Week outings are finished, and he wants to tell the matron about the adventures and the kind guardian who took him along.

faq.q: Why is Children's Week important to the Horde?
faq.answer: Decades of relentless warfare against demons, humans, and centaur have left countless Horde children without families. Children's Week is a time for warriors to step away from the battlefield and honor the future generations of Durotar and beyond.

angles.text: For the Horde, strength is not merely martial prowess; it is the collective will to protect and uplift the vulnerable who will one day carry the banner of the Warchief.
Orcish culture prizes courage and honor, and showing compassion to an orphaned child like Grunth exemplifies the nobility Thrall seeks to instill in the new Horde.
